title: Learning a better plasma ramp-down
label: Experimental control
subtitle: Learned dynamics and predict-first experiments at TCV.
source: Wang, A. M. et al. Learning plasma dynamics and robust rampdown trajectories with predict-first experiments at TCV. Nature Communications 16, 8877 (2025).
claim: The researchers trained a neural dynamics model on 311 TCV pulses, including five high-performance examples. They used reinforcement learning to design ramp-down trajectories and tested those trajectories in experiments.
limits: The result concerns a specific phase of a discharge on one research tokamak. It does not demonstrate full-plant autonomy or a measured electricity saving.
access: The repository holds a captured article and a source summary. For this draft, the note was read and the core claim was cross-checked against the publisher PDF search result. The publisher HTML retrieval failed; that is an access limit, not evidence against the study.
keywords: TCV Wang rampdown 311 pulses reinforcement learning

title: Testing learned control on HL-3
label: Experimental control
subtitle: Reinforcement learning trained in a data-driven simulator.
source: Wu, N. et al. High-fidelity data-driven dynamics model for reinforcement learning-based control in HL-3 tokamak. Communications Physics 8, 393 (2025).
claim: The study uses historical machine data to train a dynamics model, then trains a reinforcement-learning controller in that simulator. It reports a 400 ms trajectory at a 1 kHz control rate on HL-3.
limits: This is bounded experimental control. It does not establish full-discharge management, long-duration reliability, or safe behavior in every off-normal condition.
access: The repository holds a captured article and a source summary. This draft read the note and cross-checked the headline result against the indexed author-hosted paper. The publisher HTML retrieval failed.
keywords: HL-3 Wu reinforcement learning 400 milliseconds 1 kHz

title: Forecasting across two tokamaks
label: Offline forecasting
subtitle: DIII-D to KSTAR: one transfer, with clear boundaries.
source: Joung, S. et al. Explainable tokamak-agnostic ELM forecasting. Communications Physics (2026). Bibliographic identity and title as recorded in the Lux note.
claim: The Lux source note describes a neural forecaster trained on DIII-D and applied to KSTAR without retraining its weights, after physics-consistent preprocessing. The task is forecasting the onset of Type-I edge-localized modes.
limits: One source–target pair is not universal portability. Forecasting is not closed-loop suppression of an instability. Detailed findings retain the source note’s medium-confidence designation.
access: The local raw record contains Crossref metadata, not full article text. The earlier library note records checking the primary article page; this draft read that note and did not independently retrieve the full paper.
keywords: ELM DIII-D KSTAR Joung instability transfer

title: Learning from plasma diagnostics
label: Offline model evaluation
subtitle: FusionMAE and reusable representations of experimental data.
source: Yang, Z. et al. FusionMAE: self-supervised pretraining for fusion diagnostics and control. Communications Physics 9, 232 (2026). Bibliographic identity and title as recorded in the Lux note.
claim: FusionMAE uses masked reconstruction of diagnostic signals to learn representations for downstream tasks. The repository describes offline evaluation on recorded HL-3 data, including missing-signal recovery and state-related tasks.
limits: Offline performance does not establish safe closed-loop control, transfer to a different tokamak, or power-plant reliability. The note assigns medium confidence to detailed findings.
access: The raw capture is Crossref metadata. It does not preserve the article’s full text. This draft uses the existing summary and retains its access limitation; no new full-paper review was performed.
keywords: FusionMAE Yang diagnostics masked autoencoder representation self-supervised

title: Surrogate models for a fusion fuel cycle
label: Simulation · preprint
subtitle: ST-E1 tritium modeling, with unresolved source inconsistencies.
source: Yang, Simon, Yildirim, Trueba, Robinson & Shimada. Multiscale Assessment of Tritium Behavior in Preliminary Fusion Pilot Plant Design Using Surrogate Models in TMAP8. arXiv:2604.19647v1 (21 April 2026).
claim: This version uses Gaussian-process surrogates for component simulations within a larger modeled fuel cycle. The work explores tritium retention and recovery for a preliminary ST-E1 plant design.
limits: This is a simulation, not a hardware result or proof of tritium self-sufficiency. The repository records inconsistent cost-reduction, uncertainty, and temperature statements, plus conflicting design inputs. No performance or efficiency improvement is asserted here.

title: From fusion energy to useful electricity
label: Concept guide
subtitle: Why the power a plant consumes matters alongside its output.
source: Project Lux. Recirculating Power. Repository concept note, updated 12 September 2026.
claim: A fusion plant must power its own systems, including heating, magnets and their cooling, pumps, vacuum equipment, and fuel handling. Those loads affect the electricity available for export.
limits: Plasma gain, target gain, total electrical input, and exported electricity use different accounting boundaries. A better control metric does not by itself measure an improvement in plant energy efficiency. This brief introduces the distinction without assigning a plant-wide gain or efficiency value.
access: This brief draws on the repository concept note. Its quantitative plant examples have not been reverified for this draft and are intentionally not reproduced in the brief.
keywords: energy balance efficiency electricity gain recirculating power
